== Biography ==
=== Current family assessment, 23 October 2026 ===

The actual Faris book has now been inspected, rather than only its catalogue abstract. Printed p.11 uses a dotted possible connection from James of Moneymore to the American brothers; p.12 explicitly reports that evidence for Robert and his brothers’ parentage had not been found. James was the author’s identifiable County Londonderry candidate, not an evidenced father. The retrospective Irish pedigree on pp.8–9 and Samuel’s 1824 Pennsylvania will discussed on p.12 identify an Irish sibling group, including William, James and Robert remaining in Ireland, without joining it to the emigrant brothers. County setting, a compatible generation and the existing family tradition keep James a plausible candidate, but cannot sustain the earlier probable father assessment. Existing father-profile propositions only: [[Glasgow-12|Robert]] 85% → 35%; [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]] and [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] each 82% → 35%; [[Glasgow-4027|John]] 76% → 30%; [[Glasgow-4030|Mary]] 64% → 22%. All five were probable; the first four are now possible and Mary uncertain. [[Glasgow-1024|James]] remains the selected named candidate; no attachment is removed. [[Glasgow-1024|James]]’s own older father stays 18%, and [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel]]’s father stays 23%. Mary’s case additionally depends on identifying the 1779 will witness Mary Arter as the emigrant sister. Faris p.13 transmits an unnamed sister styled Mrs Arthur; p.15 identifies Mary Arter with that sister through the tax/probate cluster, rather than an explicit sibling or birth statement. The association remains positive but does not establish her father. Robert, Arthur and Joseph’s established brotherhood remains separately supported by the maintained 1806 letter transcription and Joseph’s 1831 will. John of Peters Township remains a probable brother at 83%; Faris p.15 also reconstructs the four brothers from the 1779–1780 tax/probate cluster. These sibling arguments do not identify their father. The 1824 Samuel will has been read only through Faris’s excerpt, not its manuscript. The Irish Robert in that will/pedigree is not identified as the emigrant Robert born in 1749. All mothers, upstream ancestry, life dates and current attachments are preserved; no live WikiTree save or identity merge follows. Exact percentages are subjective pair-specific judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied probabilities.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990), printed pp.8–15; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FN-6 pp.10–11], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FV-S pp.14–15]; FamilySearch film 2055438 Item 5, DGS 007834162, images 1564–1567, visually inspected 23 October 2026. Published genealogy, not newly inspected original wills or letters.</ref>


'''Mary Glasgow''', later identified in a published family reconstruction as '''Mary Arter''', is named as a sister of [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]]. Her identity, dates and later life have not yet been established from a record that expressly states the relationship.

'''Earlier research argument, superseded for fatherhood on 23 October 2026:'''
David Faris's genealogy describes Robert as a son of “James Glasgow of Moneymore” and states that Robert emigrated in 1769 with three brothers and one sister.<ref name="Faris">David Faris, ''The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio: A Genealogy of the Descendants of Robert Glasgow (1749–1839) and His Wife Rosanna of Bush Creek, Adams County, Ohio'' (Baltimore: Gateway Press, 1990), especially pp. 14–15; [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 WorldCat catalogue record and summary].</ref>

Faris discusses the 1779 Peters Township tax and probate cluster containing John, Robert, Arthur and Joseph Glasgow. John's will was witnessed by Joseph Glasgow, James Neely and '''Mary Arter'''. Faris concludes that John, Joseph, Robert and Arthur were the four brothers and that Mary Arter was their sister.<ref name="JohnWill">Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, p. 161, will of John Glasgow of Peters Township, dated 14 March and proved 3 September 1779; [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm published will-book index]. The abstract establishes Mary Arter as a witness but does not state that she was John's sister.</ref>

The family reconstruction therefore identifies the emigrant siblings as:

* [[Glasgow-4027|John Glasgow of Peters Township]];
* [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]];
* [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph Glasgow]];
* [[Glasgow-649|Arthur Glasgow]]; and
* Mary Glasgow, possibly the witness Mary Arter.

A later Adams County account independently calls John a brother of Joseph, Robert and Arthur, and says the three surviving brothers moved to Virginia after John's death.<ref name="AdamsCounty">Joyce Wilson, “Our Ancestors of Adams County,” ''People's Defender'', 29 March 2024, [https://www.peoplesdefender.com/2024/03/29/our-ancestors-of-adams-county-3/ online article].</ref> It does not mention Mary.

The will and tax cluster makes the identification of Mary Arter a useful and geographically specific hypothesis. It is not direct proof: the will calls her a witness, not a sister, and no located marriage or other record yet demonstrates that a woman born Mary Glasgow became Mary Arter.

No located record presently:

* gives Mary's age or exact birthplace;
* expressly calls her a sister of Robert, Arthur, Joseph or John;
* names her parents;
* identifies her Arter husband or any child; or
* traces her after the 1779 will.

Her birth is entered as before 1769 only because the family tradition places the sister in the 1769 migration party. County Londonderry is uncertain and inferred from Robert's sworn statement that he was born there.<ref name="RobertPension">Revolutionary War pension application R4057, Robert Glasgow, [https://revwarapps.org/r4057.pdf transcription and file extracts]. Robert's declaration gives his own County Derry birth and 1769 migration but names no parent or sibling.</ref>

=== Proposed parents ===

[[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow]] and [[Harkness-1149|Mary Harkness]] are attached as uncertain parents to represent the existing family hypothesis. Faris names James of Moneymore as Robert's father but does not name the sister's parents or the father's wife. Mary Harkness derives from later compiled pedigrees and remains unsupported by an independently located family record.

=== Research priorities ===

* Inspect Faris's complete citations and underlying family papers for the basis of the Mary Arter identification.
* Inspect the original 1779 will and John Glasgow's probate packet for every occurrence of Mary Arter.
* Reconstruct the Arter households of Peters Township, Cumberland County, and nearby Cecil County to identify Mary's husband, residence and maiden name.
* Search Nottingham/Cecil County church, land, probate and marriage records for a Mary Glasgow or Mary Arter in the immigrant network.
* Locate the original 1806 Joseph-and-Betty-to-Arthur letter and check it for references to a sister or her descendants.

The family association is positive but the witness-to-sister identification remains inferential.

Complete selected father-profile proposition; recorded role and adult identification distinguished below.
